Use `budget.spent` as each line's total instead of summing expense `cost`.

For budget lines whose total expense cost (summing `cost` by `link_to_budget`) is above the average spend per budget line, what is their average total, how many expenses do they have altogether, and on average by how much do they exceed that average? queries:
WITH totals AS (
    SELECT link_to_budget, SUM(cost) AS total_cost, COUNT(*) AS expense_count
    FROM expense
    WHERE link_to_budget IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY link_to_budget
),
avg_total AS (
    SELECT AVG(total_cost) AS avg_cost FROM totals
)
SELECT AVG(t.total_cost) AS average_total,
       SUM(t.expense_count) AS total_expenses,
       AVG(t.total_cost - a.avg_cost) AS average_excess
FROM totals t, avg_total a
WHERE t.total_cost > a.avg_cost;
WITH totals AS (
    SELECT link_to_budget, SUM(cost) AS total, COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM expense
    GROUP BY link_to_budget
),
avg_spent AS (
    SELECT AVG(spent) AS a FROM budget
)
SELECT AVG(total) AS avg_total,
       SUM(cnt) AS num_expenses,
       AVG(total - (SELECT a FROM avg_spent)) AS avg_excess
FROM totals
WHERE total > (SELECT a FROM avg_spent);
WITH t AS (
    SELECT b.budget_id,
           COALESCE(SUM(e.cost), 0) AS total,
           COUNT(e.expense_id) AS cnt
    FROM budget b
    LEFT JOIN expense e ON e.link_to_budget = b.budget_id
    GROUP BY b.budget_id
),
a AS (
    SELECT AVG(total) AS avg_total FROM t
)
SELECT AVG(t.total) AS average_total,
       SUM(t.cnt) AS total_expenses,
       AVG(t.total - a.avg_total) AS average_excess
FROM t, a
WHERE t.total > a.avg_total;
SELECT
  (SELECT AVG(b.spent) FROM budget b WHERE b.spent > (SELECT AVG(spent) FROM budget)) AS avg_total,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM expense e JOIN budget b ON e.link_to_budget = b.budget_id WHERE b.spent > (SELECT AVG(spent) FROM budget)) AS expense_count,
  (SELECT AVG(b.spent - (SELECT AVG(spent) FROM budget)) FROM budget b WHERE b.spent > (SELECT AVG(spent) FROM budget)) AS avg_excess;
